blocking.section: Distributed state catalog > State client and RZ-STS error codes
blocking.issue: Only partly resolved. The registry now gives 502 for a response Phase, but it still gives 503 for every request-Phase failure. Pack 8.10 requires 401 or 403 when a closed failure happens in a request Phase for auth and authz types, and WASM plugin system follows the pack. A `plugin` Policy with `filterClass` auth or authz is closed only and may make its one blocking `state_get` in `onRequestHeaders`. When that call fails, this document requires 503 while pack 8.10 and 05 require 403. That contradicts the foundation pack and a sibling document.
blocking.evidence: Line 336: "Before commit, a code returns 503 in a request Phase and replaces the response with 502 in a response Phase". Lines 340-344: Status "503 or 502" for every code. Pack 8.10: "| A request Phase, `onRequestHeaders` to `onUpstreamRequest` | 401 or 403 for auth and authz types, otherwise 503; code per section 8.6 |". 05 line 386: "filterClass: authz          # closed only: a trap or timeout rejects with 403". 05 line 103: "A negative guest result uses `RZ-STS` only when its State Store call was attempted and failed or timed out".
blocking.fix: Failure scenario: an authz-class Plugin in `onRequestHeaders` calls `state_get` while its shard breaker is open. This document returns 503 RZ-STS-003, but pack 8.10 and 05 return 403 with an RZ-STS code. Clients and conformance tests then disagree, and client retry behavior differs (a 503 is retried, a 403 is not). Fix, word-neutral: change line 336 to "Before commit, a code takes pack 8.10's status: 401 or 403 for auth and authz types and 503 otherwise in a request Phase, and 502 in a response Phase". Change the Status column to "Per pack 8.10".

blocking.section: High availability > Ruralz Control availability; Distributed state catalog (Published Node count row); Chaos experiments (CE-7, CE-10)
blocking.issue: This is a regression from the L4X-2 fix. The new rule lets the published Node count fall when a qualified Node misses three heartbeats. Heartbeats run every 15 s (target), so the rule fires after about 45 s. After every replica restarts, or after a replica or the leader is lost, Nodes redial with full-jitter backoff up to 60 s. Per-replica stream admission also sheds them, and CE-10 itself allows 5 minutes to reconnect. Many qualified Nodes are therefore silent for more than three heartbeat intervals only because Ruralz Control restarted. The rule lowers the count anyway ('large decreases publish at once'), which is the collapse the fix was meant to prevent. CE-10's 'drops at most 10%' criterion cannot pass as the mechanism is specified. The text also never says when the missed-heartbeat clock starts for a replica that has just restarted with no heartbeat aggregates, which are held in memory and rebuilt by resync.
blocking.evidence: Line 179: "Only qualified Nodes missing three heartbeats may lower it, with qualification keyed by `node.id` in committed state". 04 line 376: "Nodes heartbeat every 15 s (target)". 04 line 385: "Backoff with full jitter, base 1 s, cap 60 s (target)." 04 line 383: "A per-replica token bucket on new streams answers excess with `Reconnect` or `RZ-CP-010`." 04 line 484: "Heartbeat aggregates, stream state | Memory; rebuilt by resync". Line 605: "| CE-10 | Every Ruralz Control replica restarted at once | All Nodes reconnect within 5 minutes (target); the published count drops at most 10% (target)".
blocking.fix: Failure scenario: 10,000 Nodes, and all three replicas restart. With the 60 s backoff cap and stream shedding, about half of the Nodes reconnect after more than 45 s. Each is counted as missing three heartbeats, so the count drops about 50% at once and derived ceilings double. Hot keys reach GCRA twice as often, and CE-10 fails. Fix: (1) At line 179, state that the missed-heartbeat clock starts only after a replica has been up and not stale for a reconnect grace of 5 minutes (target), matching CE-10. Before that, no decrease caused by missed heartbeats publishes. The replica loss and leader failover cases (CE-7) get the same rule. (2) Put the same grace in the catalog row and in option (a) of OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-14. (3) The word band has only about 15 words of room (6,485 of 6,500 words), so condense other prose to make space, without removing text that resolved earlier findings.

blocking.section: Horizontal scaling > Autoscaling signals; High availability > Ruralz Control availability; Multi-region > Topologies (Home Region loss); Chaos experiments (CE-17)
blocking.issue: The L4X-1 fix added capacity that has to exist before a failure: pre-provisioning for R / (R − 1) of each Region's peak share, plus 30% headroom above peak for a Ruralz Control outage. The autoscaling rule in the same document removes that capacity. Scale-in happens when every signal is under half its threshold, and nothing sets an autoscaler minimum at the pre-provisioned count. When the home Region or Ruralz Control is lost, new Nodes cannot enroll, so capacity removed by scale-in cannot come back. This hidden single point of failure makes CE-17 depend on the autoscaler being off.
blocking.evidence: Line 141: "Scale out on the first signal over its threshold; scale in only when all are under half of it." Line 145: "80% × (Z − 1) / Z over 2 minutes for Z zones: 40% at two, 53% at three". Line 392: "each active-active Region SHOULD be pre-provisioned for R / (R − 1) times its peak share (target): 100% of global peak each with two Regions". Line 181: "autoscaling adds nothing during a long outage; Clusters SHOULD keep 30% headroom above peak (target)". Line 612: "| CE-17 | Home Region lost with every voter | The surviving Region serves full peak on pre-provisioned Nodes (target)".
blocking.fix: Failure scenario: two Regions with three zones each. Each Region is pre-provisioned to carry 100% of global peak, so at its own 50% peak share it runs at about half the CPU that full load would give, about 26% against the 53% threshold. All signals are under half their thresholds (26.5% CPU), so the autoscaler scales in and removes the Region-loss capacity every day. The home Region is then lost. Enrollment stops (`RZ-CP-004`), autoscaled replacements stay not ready, and the survivor runs at about 2x its CPU with in-flight units saturated, returning 503 `RZ-RT-005`. Fix: (1) Add to Autoscaling signals: "Autoscaler minimums MUST hold the pre-provisioned and headroom Node count (target); scale-in never goes below it." (2) Run CE-17 with the autoscaler enabled, after an off-peak scale-in period.

non_blocking.section: Stateless data plane; Limits and bottlenecks > Per-Node limits
non_blocking.suggestion: The Quota denial cache (line 69) is bounded only by a 60 s TTL per key and has no entry cap, which falls short of SG-7. A `quota` Policy with a high-cardinality `config.key` can grow it without limit under a 100x load of distinct keys. Either give it an entry cap inside the shared 1,048,576-entry key table, or state its maximum size (target). L1 raised the same point.

non_blocking.section: Distributed state catalog > State client and RZ-STS error codes
non_blocking.suggestion: Calls are counted in flight 'until its reply or a connection reset'. After a failover to a new primary address, calls on black-holed old connections may never get a reset until TCP retransmissions time out, which can take minutes. State how the State client detects dead connections, for example a write timeout or periodic PING (target), so that hung calls and half-open probes cannot fill the Node-wide 8,192 in-flight ceiling and spread one shard's failure to every shard.
Tag the timing figures on line 179: 'under 10 minutes old' and 'three heartbeats' (target), as the style guide requires for the 10-minute qualification elsewhere.

After home Region loss, a surviving relay goes stale and sends `Reconnect` (`rebalance`) after 30 s (target), so its Nodes redial in a loop with nowhere healthy to go. Say that this churn is expected, stays off the request path, and is bounded by the Control Stream backoff cap of 60 s (target).
The body is 6,485 words against a 6,500 maximum. The fixes for L4X-14, L4X-18 and L4X-19 have to be word-neutral or offset by condensing other prose. Do not cut text that resolved earlier findings.
